raw_case_text:
A 24-year-old male resident of the metropolitan region of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, was referred to the Leprosy Outpatient Clinic by the primary care service on account of diffuse skin lesions over the body, which began 10 months previously. Past medical history: yellow fever 4 years previously, was a non-drinker and non-smoker, and said he did not use medications regularly. He said there was no history of leprosy in his family. A dermatological evaluation identified >20 diffuse lesions over the body (face, upper limbs, lower limbs, and trunk) in the form of papules, nodules, and tubercles. A Mitsuda test and bacilloscopy were requested, which were positive (5 mm) and 5.25, respectively, and MDT for MB leprosy was started after classification of the borderline lepromatous form (BL/LL). The patient was assessed by a neurologist at the beginning of treatment despite not having neurological symptoms, and a neurological examination did not show nerve thickening or sensory or motor changes.
After 4 months of MDT, the patient returned to the neurologist claiming he had been suffering from paresthesia in the fourth and fifth fingers of the left hand for ~1 month. On examination, the patient had pain upon palpation in the region above the left elbow and thickening of the ulnar nerve, associated with tactile hypoesthesia, thermal and pain insensitivity, and grade 4 muscle weakness according to the Medical Research Council (MRC) Scale in the hypothenar region (little finger abductor and first dorsal interosseous muscles). A nerve conduction study (NCS) showed an absence of sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) in the left ulnar nerve and a reduced amplitude of compound motor action potentials (CMAPs) with a conduction block and reduced motor speed in the elbow segment (Table 1). Other nerves did not show alterations upon clinical examination and an NCS. Acute neuritis of the left ulnar nerve type 1 reaction was diagnosed.
The neuromuscular ultrasound (NMUS) evaluation showed marked ulnar thickening, measuring 24 mm2 at the epicondylar level and 92 mm2 at the supraepicondylar level [reference value (RV): 8 mm2], as well as homogeneous fascicular hypoechogenicity and vascular flow on the Power Doppler (Note: Power Doppler is more sensitive than the Color Doppler for detecting blood flow, but it does not provide information on the direction of flow). Ultrasound-guided local injection of 40 mg methylprednisolone with lidocaine was performed every 2 weeks above the elbow groove where the ulnar nerve was most damaged.
The patient was followed up in neurological appointments every 2 weeks, and after 2 months, the patient was reassessed and there was no complaint of paresthesia or pain upon neurological examination, an MRC grade 5 was determined in all muscles, and a subjective reduction in neural thickening was noted. An NCS was repeated within 3 months after the start of corticosteroid therapy and an improvement in electrophysiological values was observed (Table 1). NMUS showed an improvement in echogenicity and fascicular disarray, a 50% reduction in the cross-sectional diameter at the two levels described above, and no flow in the Power Doppler (Figure 1).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 24-year-old male from metropolitan Rio de Janeiro presented with diffuse skin lesions over his body of 10 months' duration, and subsequently developed left fourth and fifth finger paresthesias 4 months after starting treatment.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was referred from primary care for diffuse cutaneous lesions present for 10 months without initial neurological symptoms. Four months after initiating multibacillary therapy, he returned to the neurologist reporting a 1-month history of paresthesia affecting the fourth and fifth digits of the left hand.
subjective.past_medical_history: He had a history of yellow fever 4 years prior. He was a non-smoker and non-drinker, took no regular medications, and reported no family history of leprosy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Negative for baseline neurological symptoms at initial presentation; positive for left ulnar distribution paresthesias at 4-month follow-up.

objective.physical_examination: Initial dermatological examination revealed more than 20 diffuse cutaneous lesions (papules, nodules, and tubercles) across the face, upper and lower limbs, and trunk, while baseline neurological examination showed no nerve thickening, sensory loss, or motor deficits. At 4-month follow-up, neurological examination revealed tenderness on palpation above the left elbow, thickening of the left ulnar nerve, tactile hypoesthesia, thermal and pain insensitivity, and Medical Research Council (MRC) grade 4 muscle weakness in the left hypothenar muscles (abductor digiti minimi and first dorsal interosseous), with all other peripheral nerves clinically normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial Mitsuda test was positive (5 mm). At 4 months, nerve conduction studies (NCS) demonstrated absent sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) in the left ulnar nerve and reduced compound motor action potential (CMAP) amplitude with conduction block and slowed motor conduction velocity across the elbow segment, while other nerves were normal. Neuromuscular ultrasound (NMUS) revealed marked left ulnar nerve thickening measuring 24 mm2 at the epicondylar level and 92 mm2 at the supraepicondylar level (reference value: 8 mm2), homogeneous fascicular hypoechogenicity, and increased intraneural vascular flow on Power Doppler.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Initial slit-skin smear bacilloscopy was positive with a bacillary index of 5.25, establishing borderline lepromatous/lepromatous (BL/LL) multibacillary leprosy, complicated after 4 months of multibacillary multidrug therapy (MDT) by acute left ulnar neuritis secondary to a Type 1 leprosy reaction. In addition to ongoing MB-MDT, the patient was treated with ultrasound-guided perineural injections of methylprednisolone 40 mg with lidocaine above the left elbow groove every 2 weeks. At 2-month neurological follow-up, paresthesia and pain had completely resolved, muscle strength recovered to MRC grade 5 across all muscles, and neural thickening decreased; repeat NCS at 3 months confirmed electrophysiological improvement, and repeat NMUS demonstrated improved fascicular echogenicity, a 50% reduction in cross-sectional area at both levels, and resolution of Power Doppler flow.
